lab: Open the unit-circle demo. Set the angle to 30°, 90°, 180°, and 270°. Record the coordinates at each angle and describe how each pair corresponds to the point’s position.
A circle has radius 8 cm and a marked arc 10 cm long. Calculate its angle in radians, then convert that angle to degrees (nearest tenth). Show the steps and units.
Set the explorer to 45°, then 405° and −315°. What do you notice about their coordinates? Explain using full revolutions.
Compare 60° with radii 1 and 3 in the explorer. What changes, and what remains fixed? Explain why sine and cosine can be defined using the unit circle.
Open Circle to Wave. Identify the vertical coordinate at angles 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°, and 360°. How do these values determine the sine graph?

A Ferris wheel has radius 15 m, and a passenger starts at the rightmost point of the wheel. After a counterclockwise rotation of 2π/3 radians, what is the passenger’s vertical displacement relative to the center? Give an exact answer and an approximate value.
Explain to a student who missed class why 180° equals π radians. Describe the geometric relationship between angle, radius, and arc length.
quiz: Keep track of the negative sign.
Find a positive coterminal angle with −50° between 0° and 360°.
A radius-8 cm circle subtends an angle of π/4 radians. Find the arc length in cm.
Use s = rθ with θ in radians.
At θ = π/3, what is cos θ?
At θ = 5π/6, what is sin θ?
The reference angle is π/6; check the quadrant sign.
At θ = 5π/4, what is cos θ?
This is a 45° reference angle in quadrant III.
A wheel makes one rotation every 4 seconds. Find its angular speed in radians per second.
How many radians are in 2.5 counterclockwise revolutions?
applications: Determine angular speed in radians per second.
Find the rider’s exact height after 8 seconds and after 12 seconds.
Explain why the height must remain between 2 m and 26 m.
At what time during the first revolution is the rider first at maximum height?
Convert the angular speed to radians per second.
How many radians does the platform turn through in 15 seconds?
How far does the sensor travel along its circular path in that time?
Explain why the sensor’s net displacement after 15 seconds may differ from its total distance traveled.
Use the Circle to Wave demo to identify the heights at quarter turns.
Describe the graph produced during two full revolutions.
Explain how increasing rotation speed changes the time between consecutive peaks but does not change the disk radius.
tryIts:
Sketch $-120^\circ$, $240^\circ$, and $600^\circ$.
Which terminal rays coincide? Justify the result using coterminal angles.
Convert $225^\circ$ to radians and $-\pi/3$ radians to degrees, and sketch their terminal rays.
A Ferris wheel of radius $12$ m makes one revolution every $40$ s. Find its angular speed and a passenger's tangential speed.

A wheel of radius $0.6$ m turns through $135^\circ$ in $3$ seconds.
Find the arc length, average angular speed, and average tangential speed.
Explain the units of all three answers.

Without a calculator, describe the point on the unit circle at
$150^\circ$ and at $330^\circ$. Which coordinates have the same
absolute value? Which signs differ?

A different wheel has radius $6$ meters, center height $7$ meters,
and period $30$ seconds. Starting from the rightmost point,
write its coordinate model and find the passenger's height after
$7.5$ seconds.
exercises:
Convert $-135^\circ$ and $300^\circ$ to radians.
Convert $11\pi/6$ and $-5\pi/4$ to degrees.
Find an angle in $[0,2\pi)$ coterminal with $19\pi/6$.
A circle of radius $8$ cm subtends an angle of $5\pi/12$. Find the arc length.
A turntable makes $33\frac13$ revolutions per minute. Find angular speed in radians per second.
Explain why sine and cosine must lie between $-1$ and $1$.
Find unit-circle coordinates at $2\pi/3$, $5\pi/4$, and $11\pi/6$.
A Ferris wheel has radius $10$ m and center $(0,12)$. Write a rider's coordinates after turning through $\theta$ from the rightmost point.

A point begins at $(1,0)$ and turns through $-7\pi/6$ radians. Determine a coterminal angle in $[0,2\pi)$ and give the exact point.
A wheel completes $9$ revolutions in $2$ minutes. Determine its angular speed in both radians per second and degrees per second.
A rider on a circle of radius $4$ m moves through $75^\circ$. Find the arc length exactly in terms of $\pi$ and approximately to two decimals.
Describe the coordinates at $3\pi/2$ and explain why a terminal point on an axis does not belong to any open quadrant.
For the Ferris-wheel model in the chapter, explain which physical quantity would change if the coefficient $8$ in both coordinate equations became $12$.
